summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to increased lethargy and low blood pressure following a recent hospitalization for urosepsis. She had been discharged on oral amoxicillin but presented again with fatigue and decreased oral intake. Evaluation revealed no active infection, with normal temperature, white blood cell count, and negative urine culture. A chest X-ray showed right basilar density, possibly atelectasis or early pneumonia, but respiratory status remained stable. The primary issue was dehydration, supported by hemoconcentration and improvement with IV fluids. Blood pressure normalized, and she became more alert. IV antibiotics were given empirically but discontinued as infection was ruled out. She was transitioned back to oral amoxicillin, advised to stay hydrated, increase salt intake, and complete her antibiotic course. Urology follow-up was recommended to address recurrent UTIs. She was discharged home in stable condition.
